text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: We should prioritize reviewing and refining our routing system because it has the biggest impact on our overall performance. By focusing on routing, we can ensure that our prompts and engines are being utilized efficiently, which will lead to better outcomes. The trade-off we're accepting is that we won't be able to review our prompts and engines in-depth at the same time, but this is worthwhile because a well-optimized routing system will have a broader positive effect. This decision aligns with our quality-first approach, as it targets the core of our system where improvements will have the most significant impact.

name: Gauge
text: Routing isn’t the bottleneck—it’s the prompts. A perfect router can’t fix a broken prompt; a bad router can’t break a good one. The real risk is optimizing the wrong layer: we’ll waste time tuning routing while the prompts themselves waste compute or misfire. Settle it by measuring prompt quality first—run a controlled A/B on the worst-performing prompt before touching the router.
